The measure aims to reduce administrative burdens and improve the ease of doing business in the country. The policy follows an amendment to Regulation 17 of the Immigration Control Act of 1993.
contextoradditionalinfo: The government introduced this measure to address administrative constraints and investor feedback regarding the business environment. By providing longer-term work certainty, Namibia aims to enhance its competitiveness in attracting foreign investment and to modernize its immigration administration to be more responsive to business requirements.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Home Affairs, Immigration, Safety and Security

policydecision_details: Announced the launch of a National Programme to Promote Collective Entrepreneurship. The initiative aims to organize farmers, fishermen, and industrialists into associations to improve production efficiency. By fostering collective action, the government intends to reduce operational costs and achieve economies of scale. The program also seeks to facilitate better access to markets for these producers. This effort is part of a broader strategy to align domestic production sectors with the country's growing tourism industry.
contextoradditionalinfo: Despite significant growth in the tourism sector and an increase in visitor numbers, domestic production sectors such as agriculture, fisheries, and livestock have not kept pace with this trend. The government identified that these sectors are currently falling short of their development potential, necessitating a structural intervention to improve organization and market integration.

policydecision_details: Announced a partnership with the World Bank to launch a USD 750 million initiative. The announcement serves as a high-level commitment between the government and the international financial institution.

Approved the Global Energy and Fertilizer Crisis Response Framework (GEFCRF) to provide financial and policy support to African nations. The framework aims to mobilize USD 5.1 billion to mitigate the impacts of rising commodity prices and trade disruptions. It focuses on four key areas: stabilizing macroeconomic conditions, securing critical food and energy supplies, protecting vulnerable households, and sustaining long-term resilience reforms. The initiative is demand-driven and tailored to the specific vulnerability and financing needs of individual countries.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced in response to significant external pressures on African economies caused by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. This conflict has led to higher global prices for energy, food, and fertilizer, while disruptions to trade routes and logistics have increased transportation costs and exposed supply chain weaknesses.

policydecision_details: Opened applications for government financial assistance for sports programmes and activities for the 2026–27 financial year. This funding is intended to support sports participation and improve public health and wellbeing. Eligible applicants, including federations, communities, clubs, and schools, must adhere to established procedures for grant processing and reporting. The initiative is supported by a revolving fund generated through a sports levy. This grant round facilitates local sports development while the government continues to manage broader funding priorities.
contextoradditionalinfo: The grants are being issued as Tonga prepares to host the 2031 Pacific Games. There is ongoing public and institutional discussion regarding the allocation of sports levy revenue between grassroots sports development and large-scale infrastructure projects required for the upcoming Games.

policydecision_details: Implemented a directive requiring Self-Financing Aggregators to refine gold dore within Ghana before it can be exported. This measure, authorized under the Ghana Gold Board Act, 2025 (Act 1140), aims to ensure that value addition occurs domestically. Export applications will only be processed upon confirmation of local refining and settlement of applicable charges. The policy seeks to formalize the gold sector and capture economic margins previously lost to overseas processors.
contextoradditionalinfo: Ghana is a major global gold producer, yet historically, much of the value chain has been captured by foreign processors. The government is pursuing a strategy to maximize national benefits from its natural resources by 2030, focusing on local value addition, job creation, and the development of a domestic gold industry, including plans for a gold village.

policydecision_details: Handed over the first batch of 60 tractors and assorted agricultural equipment to selected farmers. This initiative is part of a broader plan to procure 180 machines to mechanize the agricultural sector. The equipment is provided through a partnership with the Yonna Group, which co-finances 50% of the costs with a four-year repayment plan. The policy aims to enhance agricultural productivity, promote commercial farming, and ensure national food self-sufficiency.
contextoradditionalinfo: The government is pursuing a long-term strategy to transform agriculture from a traditional practice into a mechanised, efficient, and business-oriented sector. This effort is intended to increase production, create jobs, and reduce reliance on manual labor, thereby contributing to national socio-economic development and food security.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock and Food Security

policydecision_details: Signed six contracts for the construction of major infrastructure facilities to support the livestock sector. These facilities include community pastures, slaughterhouses, milk collection centres, and fattening and breeding schemes. The project aims to improve the livelihoods of livestock farmers and strengthen production and productivity in rural communities. By investing in these assets, the government intends to stimulate business entrepreneurship within the livestock value chain.
contextoradditionalinfo: The initiative is part of the Small Ruminant Production Enhancement Project (SRPEP) under the Ministry of Agriculture, designed to enhance the resilience and productivity of rural livestock farmers in The Gambia.

policydecision_details: Launched a local grain purchase program to support both domestic farmers and food-insecure households. Farmers are required to register their grain between August 31 and September 4, 2026, with the actual purchasing phase scheduled from September 9 to 18. The program aims to procure grain directly from farmers across all 10 districts to replenish national food stocks. Strict quality and origin requirements are in place, including the need for valid documentation verified by local chiefs or agricultural extension offices.

Issued Executive Decree No. 16 to amend the existing list of countries whose nationals are eligible to apply for the Friendly Nations Residence Permit. Specifically, it adds Ecuadorian nationals to the list of eligible foreign nationals. This permit is designed for individuals from countries that maintain friendly, professional, economic, and investment relations with Panama.
contextoradditionalinfo: Panama maintains a specific residence permit program for nationals of countries that have established friendly, professional, economic, and investment ties with the nation. The government periodically updates the list of eligible countries to reflect current diplomatic and economic priorities.

policydecision_details: Gazetted a Revised Electricity Pricing Policy for public comment to create a unified and coherent framework for the transitioning energy sector. The policy mandates that electricity tariffs become cost-reflective within five years and introduces a multi-year pricing forecast to improve transparency and planning. It establishes that the National Energy Regulator of South Africa (NERSA) will approve all tariffs, preventing licensees from charging unauthorized amounts. Additionally, the policy includes provisions for subsidizing low-income households and creating special tariffs to promote local economic development. This overhaul is part of a broader strategy to unbundle Eskom and foster a competitive energy market.
contextoradditionalinfo: Electricity prices in South Africa have risen sharply over the last decade, with tariff adjustments causing prices to double. The government is currently unbundling the state utility Eskom into three separate entities to allow for private-sector participation in the national grid. This policy aims to address the resulting need for a more transparent, efficient, and cost-reflective pricing structure to protect businesses and households from price volatility.

policydecision_details: Announced five key imperatives to transform public service institutions across the SADC region. These recommendations focus on building institutional resilience, enhancing responsiveness to citizen needs, and ensuring citizen-centric service delivery. The policy also emphasizes the modernization of processes through innovation and digital tools. Finally, it calls for strengthened integrity and consequence management to curb corruption and improve public trust.

policy_description: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations
policydecision_details: Inaugurated a technical committee to accelerate fish production in the country. This committee is tasked with reviewing previous recommendations from a 2025 strategic roundtable to translate them into concrete, actionable interventions. The initiative aims to address systemic challenges such as high production costs, limited access to quality inputs, and infrastructure gaps. By coordinating efforts across public and private sectors, the government seeks to boost domestic fish production and reduce reliance on imports.
contextoradditionalinfo: Domestic fish production in Nigeria currently remains significantly below national demand, negatively impacting food security, household incomes, and foreign exchange reserves. The government identified critical constraints including high feed costs, inadequate storage infrastructure, and limited access to finance. This initiative is part of the broader National Policy on Marine and Blue Economy to strengthen the fisheries value chain.
decision_making_institution: Federal Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy
policycategory: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations

policydecision_details: Entered into a major energy agreement with the United States to grant private corporations control over 17 strategic oil fields. This deal involves the development of 65 billion barrels of proven oil reserves, with an expected USD 100 billion in private investment. The policy includes a legislative overhaul that slashes royalties and taxes while allowing international arbitration for legal disputes. The agreement aims to secure long-term oil supply for the US and foster economic growth in Venezuela.
contextoradditionalinfo: Following the January 3 military strikes and the kidnapping of President Nicolás Maduro, the acting Rodríguez administration has pursued a diplomatic rapprochement with Washington. This shift includes opening the country's energy and mining sectors to Western companies and moving away from the state-led energy model established by former President Hugo Chávez. The deal is intended to address rising fuel costs in the US and stabilize the Venezuelan economy through foreign investment.

policydecision_details: Bolivia, Chile, Argentina, and Peru have signed a historic agreement to coordinate their efforts in the supply of strategic minerals. The agreement aims to position these nations as leaders in the global supply chain for critical minerals essential for the clean energy transition. The collaboration focuses on prospecting, exploration, extraction, and logistics of minerals such as lithium, copper, and cobalt. This initiative seeks to enhance productivity, efficiency, and ESG standards across the regional mining sector.
contextoradditionalinfo: The agreement is driven by the rising global demand for strategic minerals required for electromobility and clean energy technologies. By aligning their policies, these four South American nations aim to leverage their significant mineral reserves to influence global supply chains and economic outcomes. The move reflects a strategic shift toward regional cooperation in the face of climate change and the global energy transition.
decision_making_institution: Governments of Bolivia, Chile, Argentina, and Peru

policydecision_details: Nigeria and Thailand have entered into a bilateral partnership to enhance agricultural education and aquaculture development. The agreement involves the establishment of a standard fish farm at the Federal Cooperative College, Oji River, funded by the Thai government. This facility will serve as a hub for hands-on training, technology transfer, and skills development for Nigerian youth. Additionally, the partnership includes student exchange programs and academic collaboration between Kasetsart University and the Federal Cooperative College.
contextoradditionalinfo: The initiative aims to transform Nigeria's agricultural sector from subsistence-based farming to a technology-driven, commercially viable industry. By focusing on aquaculture, the government seeks to meet domestic fish demand and reduce reliance on imported fish products while creating sustainable business opportunities for the youth population.
decision_making_institution: Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security

policydecision_details: Approved the inclusion of wildlife crossings in new road infrastructure projects. The regulation requires that these crossings be integrated during the earliest stages of development and budgeting. Existing roads may also be retrofitted with wildlife crossings if evidence demonstrates their necessity for habitat connectivity and safety. The National Environmental Technical Secretariat will oversee the approval process to ensure plans are sufficient.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced to address the fragmentation of forests and the high rate of wildlife-vehicle collisions in Costa Rica, a global biodiversity hotspot. Road infrastructure has historically interrupted natural connectivity, threatening species such as sloths, tapirs, and monkeys. By implementing these crossings, the government aims to balance essential infrastructure development with the conservation needs of the country's wildlife, which is also vital for the ecotourism industry.

policydecision_details: Developed an action plan to guide preparedness and response to anticipated El Niño conditions. The plan focuses on early warning systems, awareness creation, and the dissemination of information regarding climate-smart agriculture and livestock protection. It aims to mitigate the impacts of climate-related food insecurity by coordinating efforts across government ministries and non-governmental organizations. The initiative is supported by the IACo V project, which provides technical assistance and capacity building for local disaster management.
contextoradditionalinfo: The Lesotho Vulnerability Assessment indicates that some communities are already experiencing food insecurity, and anticipated El Niño conditions are expected to worsen the situation. The project builds upon the successful implementation of Phase I of the IACo V project and aligns with Lesotho's 2017 National Climate Change Policy to build climate-resilient development.

policydecision_details: Initiated a strategy to promote cleaner energy and reduce transportation costs for public sector employees. The National Automotive Design and Development Council is overseeing the rollout, which includes the development of supporting infrastructure. The government aims to expand this program to further integrate alternative-energy transportation across the country.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is driven by the need to transition to alternative fuels, such as electricity and Compressed Natural Gas (CNG), to mitigate the impact of high transportation costs. The government is simultaneously investing in infrastructure, including charging stations and gas refilling facilities, to support the adoption of these vehicles. This initiative is part of a wider effort to modernize the automotive sector and reduce reliance on traditional fossil fuels.

policydecision_details: Approved maintaining a neutral monetary policy stance for the next six months. The monetary policy rate will remain at 2 percent, with the interest rate corridor maintained at 0–4 percent. Additionally, the Statutory Reserve Deposit rate will remain unchanged at 15 percent. The NRBT continues to strengthen monetary policy transmission as part of its modernization efforts to better influence liquidity, interest rates, and inflation. The bank remains data-dependent and ready to adjust policy if inflationary pressures intensify.
contextoradditionalinfo: Headline inflation in Tonga reached 9.3% in July 2026, significantly exceeding the NRBT's 5% reference rate and marking the highest level since January 2024. This inflationary pressure is primarily driven by external supply-side shocks, which have increased the cost of living for households and raised operational costs for businesses. Despite these pressures, domestic demand appears contained and foreign reserves remain adequate, supporting the decision to maintain the current neutral stance.
decision_making_institution: National Reserve Bank of Tonga (NRBT) Board of Directors

policydecision_details: Commissioned 100 modern electric mass transit buses to support federal civil servants working in the Federal Capital Territory. This initiative aims to reduce the transportation burden on workers and improve their overall welfare. The buses were assembled locally in Nigeria to support the government's 'Nigeria First' policy. This measure is intended to enhance productivity and reliability in the public service sector.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced as a direct response to the rising cost-of-living pressures facing public servants, for whom daily commuting has become a significant household expense following the removal of fuel subsidies and other economic reforms.
decision_making_institution: Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation

policydecision_details: Signed three economic and fiscal laws to improve revenue collection and fiscal discipline. The Customs Act 2026 consolidates customs provisions to simplify administration and reduce revenue losses. The Energy Sector Levies Amendment Act 2026 mandates upfront payment of fuel taxes to prevent abuse of exemptions. The Value Added Tax Amendment Act 2026 adjusts VAT administration, including an exemption for gold mining companies selling 30% of their production to the Bank of Ghana.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is part of a broader effort to strengthen Ghana's public-finance framework and fiscal credibility. Following the creation of an independent fiscal council in 2025, the government is implementing stricter budget rules and sanctions to manage debt and improve economic governance.

policydecision_details: The Cotton, Cashew and Shea Council (CCA-K) of Côte d'Ivoire has signed a partnership agreement with the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade’s textile and apparel chamber (CCPIT-TEX). This agreement aims to facilitate technology transfers, industrial expertise, and strategic investments from China to expand local cotton processing capacity. The initiative seeks to move beyond raw material exports by strengthening the domestic textile and apparel value chain. The collaboration focuses on spinning, weaving, and garment manufacturing to retain more value within the Ivorian economy.
contextoradditionalinfo: Côte d'Ivoire has struggled to increase its domestic cotton processing, with over 90% of its cotton still exported in raw form as of 2026. The government previously set a target to raise processed cotton fiber to 40% by 2025, but progress has been limited. By partnering with China, the world's largest exporter of textiles, Abidjan aims to bridge the gap in its industrial infrastructure and technical capabilities.

policydecision_details: Introduced the Authorised Economic Operator – Tonga Customs Secure Export Scheme. This voluntary accreditation programme is designed to streamline export procedures for eligible businesses. It aims to strengthen supply chain security and ensure regulatory compliance among exporters. Accredited businesses will benefit from more efficient Customs processes, reducing administrative delays and improving trade reliability.
contextoradditionalinfo: Tonga relies heavily on agricultural and fisheries exports, but local businesses face challenges in meeting increasingly complex international trade and compliance requirements. The scheme was launched to support a more secure, efficient, and compliant export sector, helping businesses navigate global market demands.

policydecision_details: Officially launched the National Apprenticeship Policy 2026–2030 to formalize and expand vocational training opportunities. This policy establishes a structured framework to transition students from education into the labor market by partnering with private sector employers. It builds upon a successful pilot program that provided training in sectors such as cookery and hospitality. The initiative aims to address national skills shortages and improve youth employment outcomes over the next four years.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was developed to address persistent skills shortages and strengthen the link between technical education and the needs of the local economy. It follows a successful pilot program initiated in 2024 that demonstrated the effectiveness of apprenticeship models in the tourism and hospitality sectors. The government identified this policy as a priority in its corporate plan to foster business growth and sustainable employment.

policydecision_details: Launched an intensified door-to-door campaign to improve urban waste management under the #Dorti Must Go initiative. The council is working with the Sierra Leone Police and authorized waste service providers to register households and businesses for collection services. This effort includes educating the public on the 2024 Sanitation Bye-Law and ensuring compliance with waste management payments. Residents are encouraged to use digital platforms like the Smart City System and the Dorti Box app to settle outstanding bills. The campaign aims to foster a cleaner city by emphasizing that proper waste management is a shared responsibility.
contextoradditionalinfo: The initiative is part of the ongoing #Dorti Must Go campaign, which seeks to address waste management challenges in Freetown. By enforcing the 2024 Sanitation Bye-Law and formalizing waste collection registrations, the council aims to improve sanitation standards and ensure the financial sustainability of waste service providers.

policydecision_details: Launched the National Single Window (LNSW), a digital platform designed to streamline trade processes for importers and exporters. This system allows traders to electronically submit applications for licenses, permits, and certificates through a single online portal. By consolidating these regulatory requirements, the platform aims to reduce transaction costs, minimize processing times, and improve the overall ease of doing business. The initiative is currently supported by 12 government agencies and is part of a broader effort to enhance trade facilitation and transparency.
contextoradditionalinfo: The LNSW was implemented through the Competitiveness and Financial Inclusion (CAFI) Project, financed by the World Bank, to address inefficiencies in international trade. Prior to this, traders faced administrative burdens by having to visit multiple government agencies to fulfill regulatory requirements. The project is part of a wider government agenda to improve the national business and investment environment, including reforms in business registration, licensing, and tax payments.

policydecision_details: Declared a national emergency in nine specific areas, including Guatuso, Turrialba, and Limón, following severe flooding caused by heavy rains induced by El Niño. This declaration empowers the government to expedite the allocation of financial resources and the procurement of services to accelerate repairs to critical infrastructure like roads, bridges, and water systems. The measure is specifically designed to address the damage caused by recent tropical waves that have impacted the Caribbean and northern regions. Authorities are also utilizing emergency logistics, including helicopters, to deliver food and essential supplies to communities that have been cut off by the floods.

policy_description: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations
policydecision_details: Formally ended the first 2026 anchovy fishing season in the north-central zone. This decision follows a scientific assessment by the Peruvian Institute of the Sea (IMARPE) which determined that environmental conditions were not suitable for fishing. The closure applies to both anchovy and longnose anchovy intended for indirect human consumption. The measure aims to protect the biomass and ensure the long-term sustainability of the resource. The decision was prompted by persistently warm ocean conditions associated with the El Niño phenomenon, which negatively impacted the biological condition and distribution of anchovy stocks.
contextoradditionalinfo: Following a temporary suspension in June, the government conducted Operation EUREKA LXXVIII to evaluate the state of the resource. The survey revealed a high proportion of juveniles and poor somatic conditions, leading authorities to prioritize resource conservation over short-term fishing activities.
policycategory: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations

policydecision_details: Advanced its decentralization process by transferring greater political, administrative, and fiscal authority to local government structures. This initiative aims to empower local authorities, such as County Councils and County Development Planning Units, to manage their own planning, budgeting, and service delivery. By bringing decision-making closer to the citizens, the government seeks to improve accountability and promote inclusive development. The process involves a gradual approach to address varying capacities and needs across different counties.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is part of a broader national agenda to enhance local governance and accelerate the implementation of the County Development Agenda. It addresses challenges such as limited technical capacity, inadequate infrastructure, and the need for better coordination between central and local government institutions.

policydecision_details: Passed a motion to establish a dedicated health fund financed through new levies, such as a communication levy, and potentially taxes on tobacco and alcohol. The Minister for Finance and the Minister for Health are tasked with tabling a Bill within 90 days to operationalize this fund. The fund is intended to exclusively prioritize the treatment of serious diseases, including tuberculosis (TB), HIV/AIDS, and cancer. This initiative aims to create a sustainable domestic source of health financing to reduce reliance on external donor support.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced in response to the scarcity of resources caused by the withdrawal of international donor funding for health programs in Eswatini. With rising health burdens and the need to meet national targets like ending TB by 2030, the government is seeking to diversify revenue streams. The proposal draws inspiration from regional models, such as Zimbabwe's health fund levy on telecommunications, to ensure dedicated funding for essential medicines and health infrastructure.

policydecision_details: Officially approved the National Upstream Petroleum Local Content Policy to guide the country's emerging oil and gas sector. The policy aims to increase local participation across the petroleum value chain by fostering business development, employment, and skills transfer. It emphasizes building the capacity of Namibian companies to compete effectively in the industry. The government intends for the petroleum sector to serve as an anchor for broader industrial development, including logistics, engineering, and manufacturing. Implementation will require collaboration between government institutions, operators, and local stakeholders to ensure economic benefits are realized.

Launched Phase Three of the Government-Business Partnership, shifting the focus from stabilization and reform to inclusive growth and job creation. The initiative aims to mobilize R3 trillion in investment to lift economic growth above 3 per cent. The partnership will expand its scope to include tourism, agriculture, agro-processing, and mining to drive industrial capacity and employment. Specific agricultural interventions include addressing water, transport, biosecurity, and finance constraints, while accelerating land reform to support new black commercial farmers.
contextoradditionalinfo: The partnership was established in 2023 during a period of economic difficulty characterized by load shedding, infrastructure decline, and greylisting. Following successful stabilization (Phase One) and reform (Phase Two), the government is now prioritizing growth to address high unemployment and improve the lives of South African citizens. The strategy aligns with the Plan for Growth and Inclusion and the Industrial Development Strategy of 2026.

policydecision_details: Approved the revised National Biotechnology Policy 2026 to leverage emerging opportunities in the global bio-economy. This policy establishes a national framework for the development, regulation, and commercialization of biotechnology across various economic sectors. It aims to enhance national competitiveness, attract investment, and strengthen food and nutrition security. Additionally, the policy facilitates Nigeria's membership in the Global Bioenergy Partnership to promote sustainable bio-based solutions.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced to position Nigeria to take advantage of global bio-economy opportunities and to provide a coordinated framework for leveraging biotechnology to accelerate sustainable economic growth and improve food security.

policydecision_details: Announced that disaster risk reduction measures related to the El Niño phenomenon will be prioritized. The government aims to strengthen preparedness and mitigation strategies to protect the country from the potential impacts of the climate event. This initiative focuses on proactive planning to minimize damage to infrastructure and agricultural sectors. The announcement underscores the government's commitment to addressing climate-related risks as a national priority.
contextoradditionalinfo: The El Niño phenomenon is a recurring climate pattern that significantly impacts Peru, often leading to extreme weather events such as heavy rainfall, flooding, and droughts, which threaten food security and economic stability.

policydecision_details: Implemented a series of engagements to strengthen the creative industry through digital transformation. The initiative focuses on sensitizing artists about the Digital Environment Roadmap, which aims to modernize the sector and improve digital literacy. Additionally, the government is conducting a formal registration of creative practitioners to build a comprehensive database for better support and resource allocation. The program also emphasizes copyright education to help artists protect their intellectual property in the digital economy.
contextoradditionalinfo: Lesotho's creative sector faces significant challenges in accessing markets, protecting intellectual property, and utilizing digital platforms for career sustainability. The government, in partnership with UNESCO and LESCOSAA, seeks to address these gaps by providing practitioners with the necessary tools and knowledge to participate in the global creative economy. This initiative is part of a broader effort to preserve cultural identity while fostering economic participation and entrepreneurship among Basotho creatives.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Tourism, Sports, Arts & Culture

policydecision_details: Approved a series of road infrastructure projects and public-private partnership (PPP) concessions totaling over N610 billion. These projects include the reconstruction, rehabilitation, and upgrading of critical highways across various states to improve national connectivity. The government is leveraging private-sector capital through DFBOM, DFBOT, and O&M models to reduce the burden on public finances. These investments aim to enhance the efficiency of transport infrastructure, which is vital for the movement of goods and services across the country.
contextoradditionalinfo: The Nigerian government is implementing a strategy to accelerate the development and maintenance of national highway infrastructure by mobilizing private-sector expertise and capital. This initiative is designed to address the significant investment requirements for road networks while reducing pressure on the federal budget. By improving road conditions, the government aims to facilitate better economic integration and logistics efficiency.

policy_description: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection
policydecision_details: The Ghana Investment Promotion Authority (GIPA) and the Ghana Union of Traders Association (GUTA) have established a collaborative roadmap to enforce the reservation of the informal retail sector for Ghanaian citizens. This initiative involves strengthening oversight and creating an inter-agency task force to prevent unauthorized foreign participation and the practice of 'fronting'. The policy enforces existing legal provisions under the GIPA Act, 2026 (Act 1117), which imposes significant administrative and criminal penalties on non-compliant foreign enterprises. Additionally, a new reporting mechanism will be implemented to allow traders to flag suspected violations of these retail market regulations.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced in response to concerns raised by the Ghana Union of Traders Association (GUTA) regarding the growing practice of 'fronting', where foreign entities operate in sectors legally reserved for Ghanaian citizens. The GIPA Act, 2026 (Act 1117) explicitly reserves informal retail activities, such as trading in open markets and small shops, for Ghanaian citizens to protect local livelihoods. The Ministry of Trade, Agribusiness and Industry convened the meeting to ensure that foreign investment remains within the formal retail sector and complies with national investment laws.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Trade, Agribusiness and Industry
policycategory: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection

policy_description: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection
policydecision_details: Extended deposit insurance coverage to include funds held in licensed electronic money platforms. Under the new legislation, mobile money wallet balances are now legally protected up to a maximum compensation of GH¢6,250. The system operates via a 'pass-through' model, where protection is provided through the aggregate trust accounts held by Electronic Money Issuers at commercial banks. This measure ensures that digital financial assets are safeguarded in the event of a financial institution's failure, without imposing direct fees on consumers.
contextoradditionalinfo: The rapid growth of the digital finance sector in Ghana, with mobile money transactions reaching GH¢3.6 trillion in early 2025, necessitated an expansion of the existing deposit insurance framework. Previously, mobile money balances were excluded from the safety net that protected traditional bank deposits. The passage of the Ghana Deposit Protection (Amendment) Bill, 2025, aims to bridge this gap and provide financial security for the millions of households and small businesses that rely on digital wallets as a primary store of value.
policycategory: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection

policydecision_details: Launched a Startup Support Window to provide grants and business development services to 75 Gambian youth entrepreneurs annually. Selected startups will receive grants ranging from USD 2 000 to USD 2 758 to support operational costs, product development, and equipment acquisition. The program also offers technical assistance, mentorship, and incubation services to foster business growth. This initiative is part of the broader World Bank-funded Gambia Resilience, Inclusion, Skills, and Equity (RISE) Project.
contextoradditionalinfo: The initiative is implemented under the World Bank-funded Gambia Resilience, Inclusion, Skills, and Equity (RISE) Project, which aims to strengthen foundational skills and create income-generating opportunities. It aligns with The Gambia’s Recovery Focused National Development Plan 2023–2027, which prioritizes sectors including agriculture, engineering, and ICT to drive economic development.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Higher Education, Research, Science, and Technology

policydecision_details: Adopted infrastructure, agriculture, and minerals as the primary pillars for regional industrialization. This strategic decision aims to foster economic growth and development across member states by prioritizing these key sectors. The initiative reflects a commitment to regional integration and the enhancement of productive capacities. Member states are expected to align their national policies with these identified industrialization priorities.
contextoradditionalinfo: The decision was made during the 46th SADC Summit to address regional economic development challenges and promote sustainable industrial growth. By focusing on infrastructure, agriculture, and minerals, the SADC aims to leverage its natural and productive resources to improve regional competitiveness and food security.

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: Officially launched the first funding cycle of the Tonga Climate Change Fund (TCCF) by signing Project Implementation Agreements for 32 locally led climate projects. These initiatives are designed to enhance climate resilience, sustainable livelihoods, environmental protection, and community preparedness across the nation. The TCCF serves as a national financing mechanism that consolidates domestic and international resources to address climate adaptation and disaster risk reduction. This milestone marks the transition of the Fund from its establishment phase to active, practical implementation.
contextoradditionalinfo: The TCCF was developed over a decade, with the concept endorsed in 2011, the enabling Act passed in 2021, and operational manuals finalized in 2024. The Fund was fully operationalized in January 2025 to manage resources from development partners like Australia, New Zealand, and the Asian Development Bank. It aims to address long-term climate risks and support community-driven adaptation, including food and water security, following a history of successful smaller-scale project rounds.
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: Issued Supreme Decree DS 5675 to reorganize the cabinet by abolishing two ministries and consolidating their functions into other departments. The decree effectively transfers the responsibilities of the former Ministry of Development Planning and Environment and the Ministry of Sustainable Tourism, Cultures, Folklore and Gastronomy to other existing ministries. Additionally, the decree introduces a new category of 'presidential delegate' to coordinate cross-cutting policies directly under the presidential office. This institutional restructuring aims to create a leaner state, although no specific savings figures have been published.
contextoradditionalinfo: President Rodrigo Paz announced a plan to shrink the cabinet from 14 to 12 ministries as part of an austerity effort to improve government efficiency. The decree was issued following public criticism regarding the delay in implementing the promised cuts, as the ministries remained operational for over a week after the initial announcement. The move reflects a broader effort to centralize administrative control and address fiscal concerns in the context of the country's economic environment.

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: Issued an advisory to all Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) to implement proactive measures to withstand climate-related impacts, in view of El Niño intensity peak. This initiative aims to ensure the continuity and resilience of business operations in the face of changing environmental conditions. The government emphasizes the importance of climate adaptation strategies for the private sector. Businesses are encouraged to integrate these measures to maintain operational stability.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is driven by heightened government concern over the increasing frequency and severity of climate change impacts in Lesotho. By advising MSMEs to prepare, the government seeks to mitigate potential economic disruptions caused by climate-related hazards. This reflects a broader national commitment to building climate resilience across the business sector.
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: The Cabinet of Ministers of Kyrgyzstan has approved a new mandatory accreditation procedure for all individuals and legal entities engaged in medical practice. State healthcare organizations will have their accreditation costs covered by the republican budget through the State Guarantees Program. Conversely, private medical institutions and individual practitioners are required to self-fund their accreditation process. The Ministry of Health has been tasked with overseeing the implementation of these new regulatory standards. The resolution was signed on August 3, 2026, and takes effect 10 days later.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy aims to standardize medical practice and ensure quality control across both public and private healthcare sectors in Kyrgyzstan. By formalizing the accreditation process, the government seeks to improve the oversight of medical services provided to the population.

policydecision_details: Bangladesh Bank issued a consolidated circular on foreign exchange regulations concerning import transactions. This document updates and replaces previous instructions, consolidating them into a single regulatory framework. The circular covers various aspects of import trade, including registration, online reporting, regulatory frameworks, and payment methods. The instructions are valid for one year from the date of issuance.
contextoradditionalinfo: The circular serves to streamline and consolidate existing foreign exchange regulations for imports, ensuring that all authorized dealers have a unified reference point for compliance. It replaces the previous consolidated circular (FE Circular No. 33, dated August 14, 2025) to incorporate subsequent updates and maintain regulatory clarity.

policydecision_details: Prioritized the upgrading and construction of tarmac roads across the country. This initiative aims to improve connectivity between districts and enhance overall mobility for the population. By developing better road infrastructure, the government intends to stimulate economic growth and promote the tourism sector. The project reflects a commitment to integrity and efficiency in public service delivery.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is driven by the need to overcome geographical barriers to connectivity in Lesotho, which hinders economic integration and limits the potential of the tourism industry. Improved road networks are seen as essential for linking districts and facilitating the movement of goods and people.

policydecision_details: Decree 163/2026 establishes a new regulatory framework for the importation and assembly of electric vehicles in Cuba. It replaces percentage-based customs duties with fixed tax quotas based on the declared value of the vehicle. The policy provides preferential tax treatment for electric vehicles and those imported with renewable energy charging infrastructure. Additionally, it authorizes both state and private entities to engage in the local assembly of vehicles using legally acquired parts. These measures aim to modernize the country's transportation sector and promote the use of renewable energy.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is part of a broader strategy to transform Cuba's energy matrix and address the severe energy crisis currently affecting the population. By incentivizing electric mobility and renewable energy integration, the government seeks to reduce dependence on traditional fuel sources and modernize the national transport system.

policydecision_details: Authorized small and medium enterprises, self-employed workers, and non-profit institutions to manage cafeterias within the Family Care System (SAF). This reform allows non-state actors to operate dining facilities for vulnerable populations while maintaining the program's subsidized nature. The measure aims to improve service quality and sustainability in the face of the state's inability to manage the program alone. Managers are required to provide two daily meals and meet strict nutritional and infrastructure standards.
contextoradditionalinfo: Cuba is currently facing its worst food crisis in decades, with nearly 97% of the population lacking adequate access to food. The state's social assistance programs have struggled to remain operational, often requiring international aid, such as recent support from the World Food Program. This policy is part of a broader package of 176 economic measures intended to increase private sector participation in traditionally state-run activities to mitigate the deepening economic crisis.

policydecision_details: Launched a strategic initiative to double bixa production by expanding the number of growers and fully utilizing the country's 3,000-tonne annual processing capacity. The Agriculture and Food Authority (AFA) will coordinate the distribution of certified seedlings, provide enhanced extension services, and support the formation of farmer cooperatives. Additionally, the government aims to improve farmers' access to affordable credit through the Agricultural Finance Corporation to boost productivity. This initiative is designed to create thousands of jobs in farming, processing, and logistics while increasing rural household incomes.
contextoradditionalinfo: Kenya's bixa processing industry is currently operating at less than half of its 3,000-tonne annual capacity due to insufficient raw material supply. The government aims to bridge this gap by integrating more smallholder farmers into the value chain, thereby enhancing export potential and rural economic development. Bixa is considered a high-value commercial crop that can be intercropped with food crops, supporting both cash income and food security.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development
commodity1: Other products, not included in the other categories

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: Accelerated its transition to electric mobility as a core pillar of its economic transformation agenda. The initiative involves expanding electric vehicle (EV) adoption, investing in clean mobility infrastructure, and transitioning public transport fleets to compressed natural gas (CNG). Specifically, over 1,200 diesel-powered city buses in Addis Ababa are being converted to CNG. This strategy aims to reduce foreign exchange spending on imported petroleum products and leverage domestic renewable energy resources.
contextoradditionalinfo: Ethiopia is seeking to reduce its dependence on imported fuel to strengthen long-term economic resilience and energy security. By shifting toward electric and natural gas-powered transport, the government aims to lower transport costs, improve air quality, and reduce greenhouse gas emissions while optimizing the use of the country's expanding renewable electricity generation capacity.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: Issued an advisory circular (RCAA-AC-UAS-26-003) to establish regulatory standards for the operation of Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) with a Maximum Take-Off Weight (MTOW) exceeding 25 kilograms. This policy provides guidance to applicants on the application process, technical standards, and safety requirements for operating such aircraft. It outlines the necessary procedures for application, document evaluation, and operational demonstrations. Furthermore, the circular details requirements for ongoing oversight, inspections, and the resolution of safety concerns to ensure compliance with aviation regulations.
contextoradditionalinfo: This policy was introduced to provide a clear regulatory framework for the safe operation of heavy unmanned aircraft in Rwanda, ensuring that UAS with an MTOW above 25kg meet established technical and safety standards.

policydecision_details: Approved the Central Water Authority (Dry Season) Regulations 2026 to manage scarce water resources due to acute rainfall deficits, caused by El Niño. These regulations restrict non-essential water usage, including vehicle washing, garden watering, and sugarcane irrigation, effective from August 10 to November 30, 2026. Additionally, the Central Electricity Board will donate 100 solar photovoltaic kits to vulnerable households to improve energy savings. These measures aim to ensure sustainable resource management and support vulnerable populations during the current water crisis.
contextoradditionalinfo: Mauritius is experiencing acute rainfall deficits, with reservoir storage levels at 61.7% in August 2026 compared to 92.7% in 2025. The government is implementing these restrictions and energy support measures to mitigate the impact of the water shortage and support vulnerable households.

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: Established a new flat rate of 90 CUP per kilowatt-hour for electricity generated from renewable sources and injected into the National Electroenergetic System (SEN). This rate applies to both residential and non-residential producers at any time of day. The measure significantly increases previous purchase rates to incentivize private investment in distributed generation. Additionally, the government has introduced tax exemptions for the importation of renewable energy equipment and for profits derived from these installations for up to eight years.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced following a severe energy crisis in Cuba, characterized by frequent deficits exceeding 2,000 MW and a complete collapse of the national electrical grid in August 2026. The state is currently unable to sustain the electrical system and is seeking to attract private investment in distributed renewable energy to mitigate ongoing power shortages.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: Increased the purchase price of wheat to Ksh. 5,100 per 90-kilogram bag. This price will be applied at designated aggregation centers where the government is purchasing locally produced wheat. The measure is intended to improve farmers' incomes and incentivize local production. It follows consultations between the Agriculture and Food Authority, cereal millers, and grower associations.
contextoradditionalinfo: The decision was prompted by a decline in domestic wheat production, which dropped from 1.7 million bags last year to an expected 1 million bags this season due to adverse weather. Additionally, farmers had previously shifted to barley production, which offered better returns, though barley prices have since declined. The government aims to reduce reliance on wheat imports by making local wheat farming more economically attractive.

policydecision_details: Increased the minimum guaranteed producer price for wheat to KES 5,100 per 90kg bag for the 2026 agricultural season. This policy aims to support over 2,000 commercial wheat farmers by shielding them from rising production costs and volatile market conditions. The Agriculture and Food Authority (AFA) is responsible for overseeing compliance among millers to ensure the price floor is upheld. This intervention is designed to incentivize increased domestic production and improve farmer incomes. The measure serves as a strategic effort to bolster national food security and reduce reliance on expensive grain imports.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced in response to rising costs of agricultural inputs, including fertilizer and fuel, and unpredictable weather patterns. Additionally, Kenya faces high international wheat prices due to geopolitical tensions in the Black Sea region and erratic yields in major exporting countries. By raising the local procurement price, the government seeks to reduce the foreign exchange drain caused by heavy reliance on wheat imports, which historically exceed 80% of annual requirements.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development

policydecision_details: Launched the Lakshmi Yojana, an unconditional cash transfer program providing a monthly stipend of INR 2,500 to eligible women. The scheme targets women aged 18 to 60 from households with an annual income not exceeding INR 2.5 lakh. The program utilizes Aadhaar-linked bank accounts to ensure direct benefit transfers and eliminate intermediaries. A total budget of INR 51 billion has been allocated to support the initiative's implementation. The policy aims to empower economically vulnerable demographics and improve financial equity.
contextoradditionalinfo: The Lakshmi Yojana was introduced as a key manifesto promise to address the rising cost of living and provide a financial lifeline to economically weaker sections in Delhi. By leveraging digital public infrastructure, the government seeks to modernize social welfare delivery and reduce leakage. The program is positioned as a strategic socioeconomic intervention to support households facing financial hardship.
beneficiaries: women aged 18 to 60, economically vulnerable households

policy_description: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection
policydecision_details: The Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industrialization developed Kenya's first National Intellectual Property Policy and Strategy to safeguard IP rights. The policy aims to provide a comprehensive legal and institutional framework to enable innovators, artists, and entrepreneurs to commercialize their ideas. It includes proposals for stronger IP safeguards, digital rights management, and benefit-sharing guidelines for traditional knowledge and genetic resources. Furthermore, the policy seeks to protect new crop varieties and introduce geographical indications for region-specific agricultural products to enhance their international value.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced because the absence of an IP framework has hindered the country's ability to maximize the value of local innovations, leading to piracy and economic loss for creators. Data indicates that patent applications are low, and many MSMEs operate without awareness of IP rights. Additionally, counterfeit goods account for over 10 percent of the Kenyan market, undermining legitimate businesses and public health, while the country spends less than 1 percent of its GDP on research and innovation.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industrialization
policycategory: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: Delivered a second batch of 5,000 photovoltaic systems to Cuba to support energy infrastructure. These systems are designed to provide solar energy to isolated rural homes, health centers, childcare facilities, and bank branches across 169 municipalities. The equipment features improved power output and storage capacity compared to previous donations. This initiative is part of a broader effort to enhance energy resilience in the country.
contextoradditionalinfo: The donation follows a series of severe national electrical system collapses in Cuba, including two total failures in early August 2026. Cuba has been struggling with chronic energy shortages, and this delivery is intended to help mitigate the impact of frequent blackouts. The cooperation reflects an ongoing trend of increasing energy-related support from China to Cuba.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Foreign Trade and Foreign Investment (Mincex)
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: Approved the draft Law on the Inviolability of Private Property, which aims to accelerate eviction processes and redefine conditions for state expropriations. The legislation also proposes the creation of a Federal Council to modernize the real estate registry through comprehensive digitalization. Controversial chapters regarding rural land ownership and fire management regulations were removed from the final text to secure passage. The bill now moves to the Lower House for further debate on the remaining provisions.
contextoradditionalinfo: The initiative was promoted by the government of Javier Milei as part of a broader legislative agenda focused on liberalizing property rights and administrative procedures. The proposal faced significant public resistance and protests, leading to the withdrawal of specific sections that would have relaxed restrictions on foreign ownership of rural land and fire-affected areas. The government's attempt to advance these reforms has been marked by intense legislative debate and social conflict.

policydecision_details: Extended the exemption from Customs Tax for the importation of photovoltaic solar systems and various renewable energy technologies until December 31, 2027. Resolution 180/2026 consolidates existing benefits and introduces new tax incentives for social investments and the marketing of renewable technologies. The measure covers a wide range of equipment, including solar heaters, wind turbines, and electric vehicle chargers. Additionally, it provides tax exemptions on profits and personal income for investments in renewable energy sources for self-consumption or supply to the national grid. The policy aims to promote energy efficiency and support the transition to renewable energy sources across the country.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is part of a broader effort by the Cuban government to promote renewable energy generation and energy efficiency. It builds upon previous regulations, such as Resolution 169/2025 and Resolution 41/2026, which established the initial framework for tariff exemptions and tax incentives. The government seeks to encourage both state and non-state actors to invest in renewable energy to address energy challenges and support social development projects.

policydecision_details: Established maximum retail and wholesale prices for essential food items, including eggs, oil, powdered milk, sugar, and sausages. The measure, formalized under Agreement No. 127, also sets a maximum commercial margin rate of 30% for these products. Authorities have warned that violations of these price caps will be met with penalties ranging from fines to the permanent cancellation of business licenses. This decision aims to curb the indiscriminate increase in retail prices and protect the purchasing power of the population.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced in response to significant inflation and public concern regarding the rising cost of living in Villa Clara. Despite the national government's recent trend of removing price caps due to their tendency to cause product shortages and black market activity, the provincial government chose to implement these controls. The decision arrives at a time when market prices for the affected commodities have already significantly exceeded the newly established ceilings.
decision_making_institution: Provincial Council of the People's Power of Villa Clara
commodity1: Others meat or animal derived products
additionalcommodities: Rice (all)|Other oilcrops, oilseeds and oil-meals|Milk and dairy products|Sugar (cane, beet and refined)

policydecision_details: Reimplemented maximum price controls on essential food items. This decision follows a broader, failed attempt at price liberalization initiated by the National Assembly in June 2026. The measures set specific price caps for products including eggs, oil, and powdered milk. These controls were introduced in response to rapid inflation and market instability that occurred after the initial liberalization attempt.
contextoradditionalinfo: The Cuban government previously attempted to liberalize prices as part of a package of 176 economic measures. However, the lack of structural supply improvements and foreign currency shortages led to an inflationary spike, forcing provincial governments to revert to price caps to manage the cost of living. Economists have criticized the move as a failure in policy sequencing and design, noting that the price caps are already being ignored in local markets.
decision_making_institution: Provincial Council of the People's Power

policydecision_details: Kyrgyzstan and Russia signed approximately 40 agreements totaling USD 848.6 million at the VIII Kyrgyz-Russian Economic Forum. The agreements cover diverse sectors including agriculture, industry, transport, and tourism. Key initiatives include a leasing program for agricultural machinery, the development of railway container transport, and the construction of a trout farm. These measures aim to strengthen bilateral economic ties and support domestic production infrastructure.
contextoradditionalinfo: The agreements were established during the VIII Kyrgyz-Russian Economic Forum held in Issyk-Kul to foster strategic partnership and economic development between the two nations through 2030. The Russian-Kyrgyz Development Fund plays a central role in financing these projects to enhance regional cooperation and industrial capacity.
beneficiaries: small and medium-sized businesses, farmers, logistics companies

policydecision_details: Extended its moratorium on sugar imports and frozen the issuance of all new importation licenses. Agriculture and Livestock Development Cabinet Secretary Mutahi Kagwe issued the directive to protect local sugarcane farmers from cheap, subsidized imports. The measure aims to ensure that domestic production, which has reached sufficient levels, meets national demand. This policy is intended to stabilize mill-gate prices and support the local sugar industry's recovery.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced to protect sugarcane farmers in Western Kenya, Nyanza, and the Rift Valley from financial losses caused by cheap imported sugar. It coincides with the upcoming Kenya Sugar Board (KSB) regional grower directors' elections, which are expected to fully operationalize the regulatory body under the Sugar Act of 2024. The government claims domestic production is now sufficient to meet national demand, reducing the need for imports that previously plugged a structural deficit.
decision_making_institution: Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development

policydecision_details: Imposed new sanctions on five entities and eight senior officials linked to the Cuban Ministry of Revolutionary Armed Forces (MINFAR). These measures, signed by Secretary of State Marco Rubio under Executive Order 14404, specifically target networks involved in the acquisition of military equipment and technology. The sanctions aim to disrupt the economic and repressive structure of the Cuban regime, particularly the military conglomerate GAESA. Foreign banks and companies are warned that maintaining financial relationships with these sanctioned entities could lead to further U.S. penalties.
contextoradditionalinfo: The sanctions are part of a 'maximum pressure' policy initiated by the Trump administration in 2026, citing Cuba as a state sponsor of terrorism. The U.S. government alleges that the Cuban regime uses its military apparatus to spy on the U.S., support radical groups, and facilitate operations for Russia, China, and Iran. Intelligence reports suggesting the acquisition of military drones and the deployment of Cuban soldiers in Ukraine have further escalated these national security concerns.
beneficiaries: Cuban military-linked entities, Cuban government officials

policydecision_details: Introduced a program providing free on-site product testing for farmers and food processors. This initiative aims to eliminate quality barriers, specifically targeting aflatoxins and other contaminants that have historically hindered agricultural exports. By decentralizing laboratory services and deploying mobile testing units, the government seeks to empower rural producers to meet regional standards. This move facilitates smoother cross-border trade with Kenya and the wider East African Community, ensuring products can enter formal supply chains. The policy is designed to improve farmgate prices by reducing reliance on informal middlemen.

Introduced a new tax scale for vehicle sales in foreign currency, ranging from 35% for luxury cars to 5% for imported electric vehicles. Resolution 172/2026 mandates that authorized marketing entities apply this Special Tax on Products and Services to sales made in US dollars or equivalent convertible currencies. Vehicles assembled in Cuba benefit from lower tax rates, with specific exemptions for electric vehicles sold with renewable energy charging stations. The revenue generated from these taxes will be directed to the Public Transport Development Fund.
contextoradditionalinfo: This policy is part of a broader set of new regulations governing the purchase, sale, and importation of vehicles in Cuba, aimed at formalizing the market and generating revenue for public transport infrastructure.

policydecision_details: Decree 163/2026 establishes new regulations for the transfer of vehicle ownership in Cuba, including sales, inheritance, exchange, and donations. The policy mandates that all transactions be formalized before a public notary and prohibits cash payments, requiring the use of instruments authorized by the Central Bank of Cuba. Buyers must provide a sworn statement regarding the lawful origin of their funds and their current vehicle ownership. Additionally, the Ministry of Finance and Prices has set new minimum reference values for calculating property transfer and personal income taxes. These measures aim to reorganize the automotive market and increase regulatory control over private transactions.
contextoradditionalinfo: The new regulations replace the legal framework that has been in effect since late 2024. This reform is part of a broader government package to reorganize the automotive market, which also includes new rules for vehicle importation, marketing in foreign exchange, vehicle assembly, and the promotion of electric mobility.

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: Introduced a new carbon market rule book that establishes a national carbon budget for international transactions. The policy sets a ceiling of 10 million metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent for international carbon market sales up to 2030. This framework creates a structured process for approving projects under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement. It aims to prevent the overselling of carbon credits to ensure the country can meet its own Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) targets. The guide also introduces a priority list of activities, such as renewable energy and waste management, while excluding land-use projects for the time being.
contextoradditionalinfo: Kenya has become a major destination for carbon market investments, including clean cooking and forest conservation. The government introduced this regulatory framework to improve investor confidence, ensure transparency, and protect the country's climate integrity. By establishing clear, predictable criteria, the government seeks to balance international carbon trading with the necessity of meeting national climate commitments under the Paris Agreement.
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: Announced a Sh2.2-trillion oil refinery project to be located in Lamu. This large-scale infrastructure investment aims to guarantee a steady supply of refined petroleum products for the region. The project is expected to anchor the Coast region's industrial growth and reduce dependence on imported fuel. It is part of the broader LAPSSET Corridor development, which includes pipelines and transport infrastructure to boost regional connectivity.
contextoradditionalinfo: The project is being introduced in response to rising fuel prices driven by global conflicts and supply chain disruptions, such as the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. It aims to transform the coastal region from a marginalized area into a major hub for private-sector investment and industrial activity.

policydecision_details: Announced a landmark budget reform involving the transfer of 944.2 billion Burundian francs to provinces and communes. This initiative aims to decentralize public spending and empower local authorities to manage resources more effectively. The reform is part of a broader program-based budgeting system designed to shift focus toward measurable results and local economic development. By bringing budget authority closer to the community level, the government intends to reduce administrative bottlenecks and improve the delivery of public services.
contextoradditionalinfo: Since 2022, Burundi has been transitioning to a program-based budgeting system to improve public finance management. This decentralization effort is aligned with the country's long-term National Development Plan (2018–2027), which seeks to transform Burundi into an emerging economy by 2040. The policy addresses historical challenges related to administrative capacity, accountability, and service delivery at the local level.

policydecision_details: Established new regulations under Decree 163/2026 and Resolution 52/2026 to authorize the manufacturing and assembly of motor vehicles, trailers, and semi-trailers. This policy allows state-owned enterprises, foreign investors, and authorized non-state legal entities to engage in vehicle production under strict state oversight. A Motor Vehicle Evaluation Committee has been created to approve suppliers, brands, and models. Additionally, the policy introduces tax incentives for electric vehicles, with lower tax rates for those assembled domestically compared to imports.
contextoradditionalinfo: This policy is part of broader economic reforms announced by the Cuban government during the National Assembly session in June 2026. The regime aims to modernize its automotive policy, ease import restrictions, and encourage the domestic assembly of electric vehicles to improve transport infrastructure and promote renewable energy integration.

policydecision_details: Introduced Decree 163/2026, which mandates that only vehicle brands and models pre-approved by a newly established Automotive Evaluation Committee can be imported, assembled, or manufactured in the country. This committee, led by the Minister of Transport, is tasked with overseeing the automotive policy and approving suppliers. The regulation replaces previous rules and aims to centralize control over the national vehicle market. Additionally, the policy includes incentives for electric vehicle assembly and the creation of a Fund for the Development of Public Transport.
contextoradditionalinfo: This measure is part of a five-year update process by the Ministry of Transport to reorganize the rules regarding the transfer of property, marketing, and importation of vehicles in Cuba. It follows recent economic transformations approved by the government to modernize the automotive sector and improve public transport infrastructure.

policydecision_details: Ordered the closure of 101 facilities involved in the production of illicit alcoholic beverages. The regulator has revoked the manufacturing licenses of these facilities and mandated an immediate recall of all affected products from the market. Distributors and retailers have been instructed to cease sales and return all stock to manufacturers. This enforcement action is part of a broader, ongoing nationwide crackdown on illicit alcohol production.
contextoradditionalinfo: The crackdown was initiated following severe public health concerns, with reports of over 50 deaths, 100 cases of blindness, and over 500 medical treatments linked to the consumption of illicit alcohol. The Rwanda Investigation Bureau has also detained over 50 suspects, citing the production and distribution of these substances as a significant security concern.
decision_making_institution: Rwanda Food and Drugs Authority (Rwanda FDA)
commodity1: Other products, not included in the other categories

policydecision_details: Introduced a mandatory health insurance cover for foreign visitors, requiring a minimum benefit package of Ksh.6.4 million. This framework includes specific allocations for emergency medical transportation, medical expenses, repatriation of mortal remains, mental health treatment, and prescribed medicines. The policy is implemented under the Social Health Insurance Act, 2023, and the Social Health Insurance Regulations, 2024. Qualifying insurance policies must be issued by insurers licensed under Kenya’s Insurance Act. This measure aims to standardize health insurance requirements for all inbound travellers.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced to ensure that foreign visitors have adequate health coverage while in Kenya, aligning with the implementation of the Social Health Insurance Act, 2023. It also reflects discussions on diplomatic reciprocity, with stakeholders suggesting that visitors should be subject to financial scrutiny similar to that faced by Kenyans travelling abroad.

policydecision_details: Reached an agreement with bottled water producers to reduce retail prices. Under this agreement, a pack of six bottles of mineral water will now cost 450 Djiboutian francs. This measure aims to balance the operating costs of producers with the purchasing power of consumers. The decision was finalized during a meeting chaired by the Minister of Commerce and Tourism to address rising inflation.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy was introduced in response to rising inflation and increased production costs for essential goods, which were exacerbated by supply chain disruptions and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. The government sought to protect household purchasing power by engaging directly with private sector producers to stabilize prices. This initiative is part of a broader strategy to contain the cost of living for the population.

policydecision_details: Introduced a new Education Bill intended to replace the outdated Education and Training Act. This legislative move aims to modernize the legal framework governing the national education system to better align with recent reforms. Key initiatives integrated into this new framework include the Education Upliftment Project, the national school feeding program, and expanded digital connectivity. The bill is designed to ensure the legal foundation of the education sector is responsive to current national development goals.
contextoradditionalinfo: The existing education legislation was deemed insufficient to support the various policy reforms and initiatives rolled out by the Ministry of Education over the past five years. Minister Francis Fonseca noted that the education system had outgrown its legal foundation, necessitating a comprehensive update to the law to reflect current practices such as competency-based curricula and new assessment frameworks.

policydecision_details: Announced the Sebabatso Youth Programme to support young entrepreneurs. The initiative involves the creation of a comprehensive business database to track and organize youth-led enterprises. Additionally, the government will provide capacity-building support to help these businesses access global markets. This program aims to foster economic growth and professional development for the youth population.
contextoradditionalinfo: The policy is part of the government's commitment to integrity, efficiency, and honesty in public service. It seeks to empower youth by providing the necessary tools and infrastructure to compete internationally.

policydecision_details: Officially launched the development of an Electronic Single Window (ESW) for trade. This digital platform will serve as a single entry point for traders to submit import and export documentation electronically. By replacing paper-based processes with an integrated online system, the initiative aims to simplify regulatory procedures and reduce administrative costs. The project is supported by the Inter-American Development Bank and the European Union, with a 24-month implementation timeline.

Approved a major institutional reform that reduces the number of ministerial entities from 27 to 21. This restructuring includes the merger of the Ministries of Agriculture and Food, as well as the integration of the Ministries of Economy and Planning with Finance and Prices. The reform also involves the reorganization of scientific and environmental competencies, moving them into new ministerial structures. These changes are part of a broader legislative package aimed at reducing bureaucracy and streamlining the state apparatus.
contextoradditionalinfo: The decision follows a plan to implement 176 transformations approved by the Communist Party of Cuba in June 2026. The government aims to reduce the size of the state administration to improve efficiency, although the move has faced criticism regarding the potential fragmentation of strategic policies, particularly in science and environmental sectors. The leadership emphasized that the success of these new laws depends on public understanding and participation.

policy_description: Unspecified measures for the management and conservation of natural resources
policydecision_details: Agreed to introduce the Wetlands Bill into the National Assembly. The primary objective of this legislation is to provide a comprehensive framework for the protection, conservation, and enhancement of wetlands and their ecosystem services. The Bill establishes mechanisms for managing both State and private-owned wetlands, including the integration of ecosystem-based approaches to disaster risk reduction and climate change adaptation. It also provides for the listing of wetlands under international conventions like the Ramsar Convention and mandates regular monitoring and reporting on wetland conditions.
